title: Adaptive safety gates for traffic routing (circuit-breaker for canaries)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement adaptive safety gates (runtime circuit-breakers + multi-signal adjudicator) that automatically cut or scale back canary/A-B traffic when SLO regressions are detected. Signals: p95 latency, error rate, token cost delta, throughput drop. Safety gates should work for canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes and expose tunable thresholds and hysteresis to the Console and API.
problem_statement: Current rollouts require manual monitoring and fixed thresholds. We have seen several incidents where small increases in per-token cost or tail latency in canaries were missed until customer impact. Need an automated, explainable gate that stops unsafe rollouts quickly while avoiding false positives from noisy metrics.
goals: Detect meaningful regressions across multiple signals within a short window (1-5 minutes)
Provide conservative defaults to minimize false positives while allowing teams to tighten thresholds for high-sensitivity surfaces
Support canary, A/B, and shadow traffic routing modes with consistent behaviour
Surface clear diagnostics in the Console and in audit logs for post-mortem
non_goals: Replace SRE/on-call — gates are safeguards, not full automation to remediate infra issues
Handle complex per-customer legal workflows (KMS/HSM changes) in this ticket
acceptance_criteria: A runtime policy (CircuitBreaker v1) can be attached to a rollout with signal selectors for latency, error rate, token cost, throughput
Policy evaluates signals over configurable sliding windows and applies damping (min-eval-duration, min-sample-count)
When a gate trips it performs a configurable action: rollback, throttle to X%, divert to fallback model, or mark as paused
Console shows a timeline with the trip reason, contributing signals and evidence (charts + aggregated stats), and a one-click rollback
Audit logs record trip, decision, and operator actions with timestamps and request samples (redacted)
implementation_plan: Design: define policy schema (signals, comparators, aggregation, thresholds, hysteresis, actions)
Runtime: implement evaluation engine in the routing plane (C++/Rust service) with optimized incremental aggregators
Stat tests: implement both frequentist (delta-test + bootstrap CI) and Bayesian priors for low-volume canaries
Console: UI for creating and editing policies, real-time trip alerts, manual override buttons
Ops: integrate with alerting (PagerDuty/Slack) and with rollout controller to perform actions
Security: ensure request samples in logs are PII-redacted and gated by RBAC
technical_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use sliding-window aggregations instead of single-request heuristics to reduce false positives from spikes
Implement both bootstrap-based CI for delta tests (robust, interpretable) and a Bayesian change detector for very low volume canaries — adds complexity but reduces missed regressions
Actions include graceful throttle and diversion in addition to immediate rollback to preserve availability for degraded but non-critical regressions
Local evaluation (at edge-router) reduces reaction time but adds code surface; initial rollout will run centralized then gradually move to edge for latency-sensitive customers
Expose conservative defaults (e.g., p95 latency +20% over baseline for 3 consecutive 60s windows with min 200 requests) and allow per-customer overrides
observability_and_metrics: Per-policy event stream (evaluations, breaches, actions) with counts and latencies
Breakdown by model version, region, customer, route
Signal histograms and delta timelines (baseline vs canary) for p50/p90/p95 latencies, error rates, tokens per request, throughput
False-positive rate and mean-time-to-trip tracked across experiments
E2E test harness that replays synthetic traffic patterns to validate detection sensitivity
testing_and_validation: Unit + integration tests for aggregator correctness with edge cases (missing data, bursty traffic)
Synthetic canary experiments in staging: generate controlled regressions for each signal and verify gate actions
A/B experiment in Canary Cluster with shadow mode to verify that trip decisions are consistent when policy is evaluated in parallel but not actioned
Chaos tests: inject transient latency spikes and ensure hysteresis prevents noisy rollbacks
Load tests to verify evaluation engine scales and does not add >2ms median routing overhead
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Centralized evaluation only, no automatic actions; generate alerts and Console diagnostics — 2 weeks
Phase 2 (pilot): Select 5 internal services and 3 customers; enable automatic throttle/diversion but not automatic rollback — 3 weeks
Phase 3 (gradual): Enable automatic rollback for low-risk models with conservative thresholds, expand to more services — 4 weeks
Phase 4 (opt-in GA): Expose policy templates in Console and enable per-org toggles for auto-rollback
